scope: compiler-lab optimization-pilot report for the retained ngraph-llvm-i64/0 graph pair, run against the unchanged bundle at the recorded Noble commit. Each stage keeps its own semantic and concrete status; no stage inherits another stage result. The graph-to-LLVM claims in it are Noble claims that compiler-lab consumed by SHA-256, not rechecked; the LLVM optimisation relation is the pinned Alive2 result; the native stage is concrete agreement on the frozen 24-input workload, not a machine-code proof.

replay.scope: The replay reads only retained files, reruns every check and build, and compares claim statuses, eligibility, control results, artifact identities, and the decision. Timing samples are fresh measurements.

comparison.detail: The candidate machine code equals the baseline machine code. Identical code supplies no runtime improvement.

retention.report: The report member is a projection of the run report. report_sha256 names the unprojected file, which stays outside the repository because it records build-host paths; applying the filter below to that file with jq yields a JSON value equal to the report member.
retention.filter: {schema, kind, profile, outcome, passed, detail, host_os, host_arch, contract, producer: (.producer | del(.source)), pins, tools: (.tools | map_values(del(.path) | .version |= (split("\n") | map(select(startswith("InstalledDir:") | not)) | join("\n")))), target, workload, measurement, coverage, costs_ms, decision, admission, admission_controls, stage_report, claims, identities, trust_boundaries, producer_gaps}

trust_boundaries: The producer's graph-to-LLVM claims are consumed, not rechecked. Compiler-lab cannot run the producer's Rust validator or its Lean kernel check. Compiler-lab binds each consumed claim to exact bytes through its own SHA-256 digests.
The certificate replay and the soundness of the fold rule are trusted compiler-lab code. No theorem binds them to the producer checker or its Lean model.
Alive2 at the pinned revision checks LLVM refinement for every concrete u64 input pair, with undef and poison inputs excluded. Its LLVM encoding and its SMT solver stay trusted.
LLVM code generation, the linker, and the host processor stay trusted. Native results are concrete observations on the frozen workload, not a machine-code proof.
Kernel samples come from one host and one process for each side. They establish no performance on another host or processor.
The llvm-pair lane observes 16 standard boundary input pairs. Its agreement is concrete evidence and never a universal relation.
producer_gaps: The producer identities are not cryptographic, so a consumer cannot recompute the certificate endpoint bindings. Compiler-lab binds the endpoint graphs by SHA-256 and replays the certificate.
The bundle records no proposal, emission, or validation cost.
The bundle exports one nonidentity candidate and no chained certificate candidate.
Producer verdicts are exporter-authored fields without retained checker process records.
